q21520.en: The sign shown indicates the start of a main road outside towns.

explain.short: The blue sign with the white road picture marks where a main road outside towns begins.
explain.rule: Blue sign with a white road and bridge = 'strada extraurbana principale' (main road outside towns). It stands at the start of that road; with a red bar it marks the end.
explain.trap: 'inizio' (start) is right: without a red bar the sign marks the beginning.

sceneParams.caption: Start of a main road outside towns

q21521.en: The sign shown, if crossed by a red stripe, indicates the end of a main road outside towns.

explain.short: A red diagonal bar on a place or road sign means 'end'. Here it marks the end of the main road outside towns.
explain.rule: Blue sign with a white road and bridge = 'strada extraurbana principale' (main road outside towns). It stands at the start of that road; with a red bar it marks the end.
explain.trap: 'barrato da una striscia rossa' (crossed by a red stripe) turns the start sign into the end sign.

sceneParams.caption: With a red bar: end of the main road

q21522.en: The sign shown is placed at the start of a main road outside towns.

explain.short: This sign stands where a main road outside towns begins, to tell drivers its special rules start here.
explain.rule: Blue sign with a white road and bridge = 'strada extraurbana principale' (main road outside towns). It stands at the start of that road; with a red bar it marks the end.
explain.trap: 'posto all'inizio' (placed at the start) is the correct position.

sceneParams.caption: Placed where the main road begins

q21523.en: The sign shown indicates a road with separate carriageways.

explain.short: A main road outside towns has separate carriageways (two roadways split by a central divider), so the sign tells you this.
explain.rule: Blue sign with a white road and bridge = 'strada extraurbana principale' (main road outside towns). It stands at the start of that road; with a red bar it marks the end.
explain.trap: 'carreggiate separate' (separate carriageways) is a real feature of this road type.

q21524.en: The sign shown indicates an overpass that lets you make a U-turn.

explain.short: The bridge in the picture is only part of the road symbol. The sign shows a road type, not a place to turn around.
explain.rule: Blue sign with a white road and bridge = 'strada extraurbana principale' (main road outside towns). It stands at the start of that road; with a red bar it marks the end.
explain.trap: 'cavalcavia' (overpass): the drawn bridge does not mean a real overpass for U-turns.

sceneParams.caption: Road type sign, not a U-turn overpass

q21525.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of an uphill stretch of road.

explain.short: The narrowing white lines show the road going into the distance, not a slope. Slopes are warned by red triangle signs.
explain.rule: Blue sign with a white road and bridge = 'strada extraurbana principale' (main road outside towns). It stands at the start of that road; with a red bar it marks the end.
explain.trap: 'in salita' (uphill): the picture shows perspective, not a hill.

sceneParams.caption: Not an uphill warning: main road start

q21526.en: The sign shown indicates that an underpass for vehicles is near.

explain.short: The sign does not announce an underpass. It tells you that a main road outside towns starts here.
explain.rule: Blue sign with a white road and bridge = 'strada extraurbana principale' (main road outside towns). It stands at the start of that road; with a red bar it marks the end.
explain.trap: 'sottopassaggio' (underpass): the bridge drawing is only a symbol.

sceneParams.caption: Not an underpass: main road start

q21527.en: The sign shown indicates that the road is closed.

explain.short: The road is not closed: the sign shows the start of a main road outside towns, where you can drive.
explain.rule: Blue sign with a white road and bridge = 'strada extraurbana principale' (main road outside towns). It stands at the start of that road; with a red bar it marks the end.
explain.trap: 'interrotta' (closed, cut off) is wrong: this sign only gives road-type information.

sceneParams.caption: Road open: start of a main road

q21528.en: The sign shown orders traffic to move in parallel lines.

explain.short: The sign is blue information, not an order. It does not tell you to drive in parallel lines.
explain.rule: Blue sign with a white road and bridge = 'strada extraurbana principale' (main road outside towns). It stands at the start of that road; with a red bar it marks the end.
explain.trap: 'prescrive' (orders): this sign informs, it does not order anything.

q21529.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of the start of a long straight road.

explain.short: The straight lines are just the road symbol. The sign tells you the road type, not that the road is straight.
explain.rule: Blue sign with a white road and bridge = 'strada extraurbana principale' (main road outside towns). It stands at the start of that road; with a red bar it marks the end.
explain.trap: 'lungo rettilineo' (long straight road): the straight drawing does not mean a straight road.

sceneParams.caption: Road type, not a long straight

q21530.en: The sign shown is placed near the Italian border, visible to drivers coming from the foreign country.

explain.short: It tells drivers entering Italy which speed limits apply, so it stands near the border facing them.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: 'frontiera' (border) is right: the sign is for people arriving from abroad.

sceneParams.caption: At the border, for drivers entering Italy

q21531.en: The sign shown indicates the general maximum speed limits that apply in Italy.

explain.short: The four boxes list the general top speeds for each type of road in Italy.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: 'limiti massimi' (maximum limits) is right: these are the highest speeds allowed.

q21532.en: The sign shown indicates, in the first box at the top, the maximum speed limit in built-up areas.

explain.short: The top box shows 50 next to a town skyline: 50 km/h is the limit in built-up areas.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: 'primo riquadro in alto' (first box at the top) goes with the town picture.

q21533.en: The sign shown gives 90 km/h as the maximum speed limit on secondary roads outside towns.

explain.short: The second box shows 90 next to a crossed-out town: outside towns, on secondary roads, the limit is 90 km/h.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: 'extraurbane secondarie' (secondary roads outside towns) is the right road for 90.

sceneParams.caption: 90 km/h on secondary roads outside towns

q21534.en: The sign shown gives 110 km/h as the maximum speed limit on main roads outside towns.

explain.short: The third box shows 110 next to the blue main-road symbol: 110 km/h on main roads outside towns.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: 'extraurbane principali' (main roads outside towns) goes with 110, not 130.

sceneParams.caption: 110 km/h on main roads outside towns

q21535.en: The sign shown gives 130 km/h as the maximum speed limit on motorways.

explain.short: The bottom box shows 130 next to the green motorway symbol: 130 km/h on motorways.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: 'autostrade' (motorways) go with 130 and the green symbol.

q21536.en: The sign shown gives 90 km/h as the maximum speed limit in built-up areas.

explain.short: In built-up areas the limit on the sign is 50 km/h. 90 km/h is for roads outside towns.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: '90 km/h ... centri abitati': 90 belongs to the crossed-out town, so outside towns.

q21537.en: The sign shown indicates the number of motorways in Italy you can use without paying a toll.

explain.short: The numbers are speed limits in km/h, not a count of toll-free motorways.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: 'numero di autostrade' (number of motorways): the numbers are speeds.

sceneParams.caption: Numbers are speed limits, not motorways

q21538.en: The sign shown gives 130 km/h as the maximum speed limit on main roads outside towns.

explain.short: 130 km/h is the motorway limit. On main roads outside towns the sign gives 110 km/h.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: '130 ... extraurbane principali': 130 belongs to motorways (green symbol).

q21539.en: The sign shown is found at the entrance of every town.

explain.short: It is placed near the Italian border, not at every town. A town entrance has the white place-name sign.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: 'ogni città' (every town) is wrong: this sign is at the border.

sceneParams.caption: At the border, not at every town

q21540.en: The sign shown indicates the minimum speed limits that apply in Italy.

explain.short: The red circles are maximum limits: you must not go faster. They are not minimum speeds.
explain.rule: Border sign 'ITALIA': maximum limits 50 in towns, 90 outside towns, 110 on main roads outside towns, 130 on motorways.
explain.trap: 'minimi' (minimum) is the trap: the sign shows maximum limits.

q21541.en: The sign shown indicates the number of the motorway.

explain.short: 'A' stands for autostrada (motorway) and 25 is its number.
explain.rule: Green shield 'A 25' = motorway number 25. Green means motorway; 'A' means autostrada.
explain.trap: 'numero dell'autostrada' (motorway number) is exactly what the shield shows.

q21542.en: The sign shown can be found inside an advance sign for a motorway junction.

explain.short: Advance signs for a motorway junction often include the motorway number shield, so you know which motorway you will join.
explain.rule: Green shield 'A 25' = motorway number 25. Green means motorway; 'A' means autostrada.
explain.trap: 'all'interno' (inside): the shield can be part of a bigger sign.

sceneParams.caption: Shield can sit inside a junction sign

q21543.en: The sign shown, combined with an arrow, indicates the direction to a motorway toll gate.

explain.short: With an arrow, the motorway shield shows which way to go to get onto that motorway, at its toll gate (casello).
explain.rule: Green shield 'A 25' = motorway number 25. Green means motorway; 'A' means autostrada.
explain.trap: 'abbinato ad una freccia' (combined with an arrow) turns it into a direction sign.

sceneParams.caption: With an arrow: way to the motorway

q21544.en: The sign shown identifies motorway no. 25.

explain.short: The shield says 'A 25', so it names motorway number 25.
explain.rule: Green shield 'A 25' = motorway number 25. Green means motorway; 'A' means autostrada.
explain.trap: 'n. 25' (number 25) matches the text on the shield.

q21545.en: The sign shown is found at the border with Austria.

explain.short: The 'A' means autostrada (motorway), not Austria. The sign gives a motorway number.
explain.rule: Green shield 'A 25' = motorway number 25. Green means motorway; 'A' means autostrada.
explain.trap: 'Austria': the letter 'A' is for autostrada, not for the country.

q21546.en: The sign shown indicates the number of the overpass.

explain.short: The number belongs to the motorway, not to an overpass.
explain.rule: Green shield 'A 25' = motorway number 25. Green means motorway; 'A' means autostrada.
explain.trap: 'cavalcavia' (overpass) is wrong: 'A' tells you it is a motorway.

q21547.en: The sign shown indicates the safety distance to keep from the vehicle in front.

explain.short: 25 is not a distance in metres. It is the number of the motorway.
explain.rule: Green shield 'A 25' = motorway number 25. Green means motorway; 'A' means autostrada.
explain.trap: 'distanza di sicurezza' (safety distance): the number is a motorway number.

q21548.en: The sign shown indicates a service centre 25 kilometres away.

explain.short: There is no distance and no service symbol on this sign. 'A 25' is a motorway number.
explain.rule: Green shield 'A 25' = motorway number 25. Green means motorway; 'A' means autostrada.
explain.trap: 'a 25 chilometri' (25 km away): 25 is not a distance.

q21549.en: The sign shown indicates that the next motorway junction is 25 kilometres away.

explain.short: The sign gives no distance. 25 is the number of the motorway.
explain.rule: Green shield 'A 25' = motorway number 25. Green means motorway; 'A' means autostrada.
explain.trap: 'a 25 chilometri' (25 km away): the number names the motorway.

sceneParams.caption: No distance: 25 is the motorway number

q21550.en: The sign shown indicates the recommended minimum speed that you should not exceed.

explain.short: This is not a speed sign at all. Speed signs are round; this green shield gives a motorway number.
explain.rule: Green shield 'A 25' = motorway number 25. Green means motorway; 'A' means autostrada.
explain.trap: 'limite minimo di velocità' (minimum speed limit): 25 is not a speed.

q21551.en: The sign shown indicates the start of a built-up area.

explain.short: A white rectangle with a town name marks the point where the town (built-up area) begins.
explain.rule: White sign with a town name = start of a built-up area. Placed on every road entering the town; with a red bar = end of the town.
explain.trap: 'inizio di un centro abitato' (start of a built-up area) is the meaning of this sign.

sceneParams.caption: Start of the town of Taranto

q21552.en: The sign shown identifies the place you have reached.

explain.short: The name on the sign tells you which town you are entering.
explain.rule: White sign with a town name = start of a built-up area. Placed on every road entering the town; with a red bar = end of the town.
explain.trap: 'località raggiunta' (place reached): you are arriving in Taranto now.

q21553.en: The sign shown is placed at the start of the built-up area, on all roads entering the place named.

explain.short: Every road that enters the town has this sign at its start, so drivers always know when town rules begin.
explain.rule: White sign with a town name = start of a built-up area. Placed on every road entering the town; with a red bar = end of the town.
explain.trap: 'su tutte le strade d'ingresso' (on all entry roads) is correct, even if 'tutte' sounds extreme.

sceneParams.caption: On every road into the town

q21554.en: The sign shown, if crossed by a red stripe, indicates the end of the built-up area.

explain.short: The same name sign with a red diagonal bar marks where the town ends.
explain.rule: White sign with a town name = start of a built-up area. Placed on every road entering the town; with a red bar = end of the town.
explain.trap: 'barrato da una striscia rossa' (crossed by a red stripe) means 'end'.

sceneParams.caption: With a red bar: end of the town

q21555.en: The sign shown indicates a tourist place.

explain.short: Tourist places use BROWN signs. A white sign with a town name marks the start of a town.
explain.rule: White sign with a town name = start of a built-up area. Placed on every road entering the town; with a red bar = end of the town.
explain.trap: 'località turistica' (tourist place): the colour is white, not brown.

q21556.en: The sign shown is placed to indicate the end of a province.

explain.short: It marks the start of a town, not the border of a province.
explain.rule: White sign with a town name = start of a built-up area. Placed on every road entering the town; with a red bar = end of the town.
explain.trap: 'fine di una provincia' (end of a province): the sign is about a built-up area.

sceneParams.caption: Town start, not end of a province

q21557.en: The sign shown indicates the direction to follow to reach Taranto.

explain.short: A direction sign has an arrow or a pointed end. This plain rectangle says you are already in Taranto.
explain.rule: White sign with a town name = start of a built-up area. Placed on every road entering the town; with a red bar = end of the town.
explain.trap: 'direzione da seguire' (direction to follow): you have already arrived.

sceneParams.caption: You are in Taranto, not heading there

q21558.en: The sign shown identifies a viaduct.

explain.short: The sign gives the name of a town, not of a viaduct (a long road bridge).
explain.rule: White sign with a town name = start of a built-up area. Placed on every road entering the town; with a red bar = end of the town.
explain.trap: 'viadotto' (viaduct) is wrong: Taranto is a town.

sceneParams.caption: A town name, not a viaduct

q21559.en: The sign shown indicates the entrance of a medical first-aid centre.

explain.short: The red cross means first aid, and the arrow shows where its entrance is.
explain.rule: White sign, red cross, arrow = 'pronto soccorso' (first aid). It stands at the first-aid centre; the arrow shows the way in.
explain.trap: 'ingresso' (entrance) is right: the arrow leads you into the first-aid centre.

sceneParams.caption: Entrance to first aid this way

q21560.en: The sign shown indicates the direction to enter the first-aid centre.

explain.short: The arrow under the red cross shows which way to go to get into the first-aid centre.
explain.rule: White sign, red cross, arrow = 'pronto soccorso' (first aid). It stands at the first-aid centre; the arrow shows the way in.
explain.trap: 'direzione' (direction) comes from the arrow.

q21561.en: The sign shown is placed at a first-aid centre.

explain.short: This sign stands right at the first-aid centre to show its entrance.
explain.rule: White sign, red cross, arrow = 'pronto soccorso' (first aid). It stands at the first-aid centre; the arrow shows the way in.
explain.trap: 'in corrispondenza' (right at) is correct: it is at the place, not far before it.

q21562.en: The sign shown indicates a border post with Switzerland.

explain.short: The Swiss flag is a white cross on red. This is a red cross on white: first aid.
explain.rule: White sign, red cross, arrow = 'pronto soccorso' (first aid). It stands at the first-aid centre; the arrow shows the way in.
explain.trap: 'Svizzera' (Switzerland): the colours are swapped, it is the first-aid red cross.

sceneParams.caption: Red cross on white = first aid

q21563.en: The sign shown indicates a pharmacy.

explain.short: The red cross here means emergency first aid, not a pharmacy (a shop for medicines).
explain.rule: White sign, red cross, arrow = 'pronto soccorso' (first aid). It stands at the first-aid centre; the arrow shows the way in.
explain.trap: 'farmacia' (pharmacy) is wrong: the sign means first aid.

q21564.en: The sign shown indicates the road to follow to reach the cemetery.

explain.short: The cross is red, the sign of first aid. It has nothing to do with a cemetery.
explain.rule: White sign, red cross, arrow = 'pronto soccorso' (first aid). It stands at the first-aid centre; the arrow shows the way in.
explain.trap: 'cimitero' (cemetery): a cross does not mean cemetery here.

q21565.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of a four-way crossroads.

explain.short: The cross is not a road drawing: it is the red cross of first aid. Crossroads are warned by red triangles.
explain.rule: White sign, red cross, arrow = 'pronto soccorso' (first aid). It stands at the first-aid centre; the arrow shows the way in.
explain.trap: 'incrocio a quattro strade' (four-way crossroads): the cross shape is not roads.

q21566.en: The sign shown indicates a car park reserved for doctors.

explain.short: There is no 'P' for parking on this sign. The red cross shows the first-aid centre.
explain.rule: White sign, red cross, arrow = 'pronto soccorso' (first aid). It stands at the first-aid centre; the arrow shows the way in.
explain.trap: 'parcheggio' (car park): parking signs have a white 'P' on blue.

q21567.en: The sign shown is found near a bridge that crosses the river Arno.

explain.short: The sign names the river, and it stands near the bridge where the road crosses it.
explain.rule: Waves plus 'fiume Arno' = the name of the river you cross on the bridge here. It is an information sign, not a danger sign.
explain.trap: 'in vicinanza di un ponte' (near a bridge) is where river-name signs are placed.

sceneParams.caption: Near the bridge over the Arno

q21568.en: The sign shown indicates the name of the river near the bridge that crosses it.

explain.short: The words 'fiume Arno' tell you the name of the river you are about to cross.
explain.rule: Waves plus 'fiume Arno' = the name of the river you cross on the bridge here. It is an information sign, not a danger sign.
explain.trap: 'nome del fiume' (name of the river) is exactly what the text shows.

q21569.en: The sign shown is one of the information signs.

explain.short: It only gives information (a river name). It does not warn of danger or give an order.
explain.rule: Waves plus 'fiume Arno' = the name of the river you cross on the bridge here. It is an information sign, not a danger sign.
explain.trap: 'segnali di indicazione' (information signs) is the right family.

q21570.en: The sign shown is placed where the road may flood when it rains.

explain.short: The waves show a river name, not a flooding danger. Danger signs are red triangles.
explain.rule: Waves plus 'fiume Arno' = the name of the river you cross on the bridge here. It is an information sign, not a danger sign.
explain.trap: 'allagare' (flood): the waves mean a river, not water on the road.

sceneParams.caption: River name, not a flooding warning

q21571.en: The sign shown indicates the danger of storm waves from the sea.

explain.short: The sign is about a river (fiume), not the sea, and it gives no danger.
explain.rule: Waves plus 'fiume Arno' = the name of the river you cross on the bridge here. It is an information sign, not a danger sign.
explain.trap: 'mareggiate' (sea storms): the text says 'fiume' (river).

q21572.en: The sign shown indicates that water-skiing is possible.

explain.short: The waves only stand for a river. The sign gives its name, not water sports.
explain.rule: Waves plus 'fiume Arno' = the name of the river you cross on the bridge here. It is an information sign, not a danger sign.
explain.trap: 'sci nautico' (water-skiing) is invented: nothing on the sign shows it.

q21573.en: The sign shown indicates a road with a series of bends.

explain.short: The wavy lines are water, not a road. Bends are warned by red triangle signs.
explain.rule: Waves plus 'fiume Arno' = the name of the river you cross on the bridge here. It is an information sign, not a danger sign.
explain.trap: 'curve in successione' (series of bends): the waves are not bends.

q21574.en: The sign shown gives advance notice of a tourist and hotel information office.

explain.short: The 'i' means information and the bed means hotels; '150 m' shows it is ahead.
explain.rule: Brown sign, 'i' and bed, 150 m = tourist and hotel information office 150 m ahead.
explain.trap: 'preavvisa' (announces ahead) fits the '150 m' panel.

q21575.en: The sign shown indicates that you can get information about hotels and motels.

explain.short: The bed symbol with the 'i' means information on places to sleep: hotels and motels.
explain.rule: Brown sign, 'i' and bed, 150 m = tourist and hotel information office 150 m ahead.
explain.trap: 'informazioni su alberghi e motel' (information on hotels and motels) matches the symbols.

q21576.en: The sign shown indicates a place where you can ask for information about hotels.

explain.short: The office announced by the sign is where you can ask about hotels.
explain.rule: Brown sign, 'i' and bed, 150 m = tourist and hotel information office 150 m ahead.
explain.trap: 'richiedere informazioni' (ask for information) is the purpose of the 'i'.

q21577.en: The sign shown indicates the number of hotels nearby.

explain.short: The only number is '150 m', a distance. The sign does not count hotels.
explain.rule: Brown sign, 'i' and bed, 150 m = tourist and hotel information office 150 m ahead.
explain.trap: 'numero di alberghi' (number of hotels): 150 m is a distance.

sceneParams.caption: 150 m is a distance, not a hotel count

q21578.en: The sign shown indicates the entrance of a hospital 150 metres ahead.

explain.short: A bed with an 'i' on brown means hotel information, not a hospital.
explain.rule: Brown sign, 'i' and bed, 150 m = tourist and hotel information office 150 m ahead.
explain.trap: 'ospedale' (hospital): the bed here means a hotel, and brown means tourism.

q21579.en: The sign shown indicates the hospital admissions office.

explain.short: The sign is about tourist and hotel information, not a hospital office.
explain.rule: Brown sign, 'i' and bed, 150 m = tourist and hotel information office 150 m ahead.
explain.trap: 'accettazione dell'ospedale' (hospital admissions) confuses the bed symbol.

q21580.en: The sign shown indicates that 150 metres ahead there is a hotel with interpreter staff for foreign guests.

explain.short: The 'i' means information, not interpreters. The sign announces an information office, not a special hotel.
explain.rule: Brown sign, 'i' and bed, 150 m = tourist and hotel information office 150 m ahead.
explain.trap: 'personale interprete' (interpreter staff): the 'i' is for information.

q21581.en: The sign shown indicates an unregulated pedestrian crossing.

explain.short: It marks a pedestrian crossing with no traffic lights or officer: pedestrians and drivers follow the normal rules.
explain.rule: Blue square with a walker on stripes = pedestrian crossing here, at the stripes. Stop for people crossing; never overtake a vehicle stopped for them.
explain.trap: 'non regolato' (unregulated) means no traffic lights control it.

q21582.en: Outside built-up areas, the sign shown is found after the danger sign PEDESTRIAN CROSSING.

explain.short: Outside towns the red triangle warns first (about 150 m before); then this blue sign marks the crossing itself.
explain.rule: Blue square with a walker on stripes = pedestrian crossing here, at the stripes. Stop for people crossing; never overtake a vehicle stopped for them.
explain.trap: 'dopo' (after) is right: the warning triangle comes before.

sceneParams.caption: Outside towns: triangle first, then this

q21583.en: The sign shown is found right at the stripes of the pedestrian crossing.

explain.short: This information sign is placed exactly where the crossing is, next to the stripes.
explain.rule: Blue square with a walker on stripes = pedestrian crossing here, at the stripes. Stop for people crossing; never overtake a vehicle stopped for them.
explain.trap: 'direttamente in corrispondenza' (right at) is the correct place.

q21584.en: The sign shown obliges drivers to stop when pedestrians are crossing on the pedestrian crossings.

explain.short: At a crossing, drivers must stop to let pedestrians who are crossing go first.
explain.rule: Blue square with a walker on stripes = pedestrian crossing here, at the stripes. Stop for people crossing; never overtake a vehicle stopped for them.
explain.trap: 'obbliga ... a fermarsi' (obliges to stop) applies when pedestrians are on the crossing.

sceneParams.caption: Stop for people on the crossing

q21585.en: The sign shown indicates an underpass.

explain.short: The person walks on stripes on the road surface, so it is a crossing at road level, not an underpass.
explain.rule: Blue square with a walker on stripes = pedestrian crossing here, at the stripes. Stop for people crossing; never overtake a vehicle stopped for them.
explain.trap: 'sottopassaggio' (underpass): the stripes show crossing on the road.

sceneParams.caption: Crossing on the road, not underpass

q21586.en: The sign shown is placed 150 metres before a pedestrian crossing.

explain.short: This blue sign is AT the crossing. The red danger triangle is the one placed about 150 m before.
explain.rule: Blue square with a walker on stripes = pedestrian crossing here, at the stripes. Stop for people crossing; never overtake a vehicle stopped for them.
explain.trap: '150 metri prima' (150 m before) belongs to the danger triangle.

sceneParams.caption: At the crossing, not 150 m before

q21587.en: The sign shown, if green, is placed on motorways.

explain.short: Pedestrians may not walk on motorways, so there are no pedestrian crossings there and no green version.
explain.rule: Blue square with a walker on stripes = pedestrian crossing here, at the stripes. Stop for people crossing; never overtake a vehicle stopped for them.
explain.trap: 'se di colore verde' (if green): green means motorway, where pedestrians are banned.

q21588.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of a primary school.

explain.short: It shows an adult on a crossing, not children. Schools are warned by a red triangle with children.
explain.rule: Blue square with a walker on stripes = pedestrian crossing here, at the stripes. Stop for people crossing; never overtake a vehicle stopped for them.
explain.trap: 'scuola elementare' (primary school): this is a crossing sign.

q21589.en: The sign shown allows you to overtake a vehicle that has stopped to give way to pedestrians.

explain.short: Overtaking a vehicle that stopped for pedestrians is forbidden: it may hide a person crossing.
explain.rule: Blue square with a walker on stripes = pedestrian crossing here, at the stripes. Stop for people crossing; never overtake a vehicle stopped for them.
explain.trap: 'consente di sorpassare' (allows overtaking) is the trap: it is forbidden.

sceneParams.caption: Never overtake a car stopped for walkers

q21590.en: The sign shown, if placed on the edge of the pavement, indicates a school bus stop.

explain.short: On the pavement edge the orange sign marks the place where the school bus stops.
explain.rule: Orange square with two schoolchildren = school bus (stop at the kerb, or on the bus itself). Be careful: children may suddenly cross.
explain.trap: 'sul bordo del marciapiede' (on the pavement edge) makes it a bus stop sign.

sceneParams.caption: On the kerb: school bus stop

q21591.en: The sign shown, if placed on the outside of a bus, signals that it carries schoolchildren.

explain.short: School buses carry this orange sign on the outside to warn other drivers that children are on board.
explain.rule: Orange square with two schoolchildren = school bus (stop at the kerb, or on the bus itself). Be careful: children may suddenly cross.
explain.trap: 'all'esterno di un autobus' (outside a bus) means the bus carries pupils.

sceneParams.caption: On a bus: it carries schoolchildren

q21592.en: The sign shown can indicate the stop of a bus carrying schoolchildren.

explain.short: One use of this sign is to mark where the school bus stops.
explain.rule: Orange square with two schoolchildren = school bus (stop at the kerb, or on the bus itself). Be careful: children may suddenly cross.
explain.trap: 'può indicare' (can indicate) is safe: a stop is one of its uses.

sceneParams.caption: Can mark a school bus stop

q21593.en: The sign shown asks you to watch out for children who may suddenly cross the road.

explain.short: Where a school bus stops, children may run across the road without looking, so drive carefully.
explain.rule: Orange square with two schoolchildren = school bus (stop at the kerb, or on the bus itself). Be careful: children may suddenly cross.
explain.trap: 'invita a fare attenzione' (asks you to be careful) is the purpose of the sign.

q21594.en: The sign shown asks you to be careful because there may be children who got off the school bus and may suddenly cross the road.

explain.short: Children leaving the school bus may cross suddenly, often in front of or behind the bus.
explain.rule: Orange square with two schoolchildren = school bus (stop at the kerb, or on the bus itself). Be careful: children may suddenly cross.
explain.trap: 'discesi dallo scuolabus' (got off the school bus) explains why you must be careful.

sceneParams.caption: Children off the bus may run across

q21595.en: The sign shown forbids unaccompanied children from passing.

explain.short: The sign is not a ban. It asks drivers to watch out for children.
explain.rule: Orange square with two schoolchildren = school bus (stop at the kerb, or on the bus itself). Be careful: children may suddenly cross.
explain.trap: 'vieta' (forbids): the orange sign forbids nothing.

sceneParams.caption: Not a ban: watch out for children

q21596.en: The sign shown indicates public gardens.

explain.short: The children carry school bags: the sign is about the school bus, not a park.
explain.rule: Orange square with two schoolchildren = school bus (stop at the kerb, or on the bus itself). Be careful: children may suddenly cross.
explain.trap: 'giardini pubblici' (public gardens): the school bags show it is about school.

q21597.en: The sign shown indicates that you must compulsorily give way to children crossing.

explain.short: The sign asks for extra care; it does not create a special priority order like a give-way sign.
explain.rule: Orange square with two schoolchildren = school bus (stop at the kerb, or on the bus itself). Be careful: children may suddenly cross.
explain.trap: 'obbligatoriamente' (compulsorily) is the trap: the sign is an invitation to be careful.

sceneParams.caption: Care, not a special give-way order

q21597.reviewNote: Official FALSE; drivers must still give way to pedestrians actually crossing (art. 191), so the wording is borderline.
